mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 4.5%, it indicates a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to reduced liquidity and higher borrowing costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a downturn in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp, or if the correlation between UNRATE spikes and negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) coupled with a decrease in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a shift in consumer spending from durable goods to services, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as service-oriented sectors benefit.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS increases and HOUST decreases, or if the joint behavior of RSAFS and HOUST does not show a statistically significant positive correlation with 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) over three consecutive months signals strengthening supply-side fundamentals, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO increases for 3 consecutive months, or if the correlation between INDPRO growth and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates easing inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the likelihood of monetary policy easing increases.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL decreases, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL decreases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and confidence improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases, or if the joint behavior of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not show a statistically significant positive correlation with 60-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals robust economic growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and investor sentiment improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 increases for 2 consecutive quarters, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where a high level of industrial production (INDPRO) relative to its 12-month moving average indicates strong supply-side momentum, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average, or if the correlation between high INDPRO levels and positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
